A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCoRe research despite the changed title and format. All 21 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCoRe benchmark results, component ablations, training-data scaling experiments, and analysis of teacher interventions and hard examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original SCoRe experiments and adds teacher-guided baseline comparisons, a DPO comparison, and manual analysis of previously unsolved cases.

M1.justification: The stated auxiliary reward is refined: v1 rewards avoiding the original erroneous action, whereas v3's Rformat additionally requires correctly formatted output. The underlying BC initialization, student-generated trajectories, earliest-error correction, correction-based SFT, and short-horizon GRPO procedure remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions list the same training sources and mathematical reasoning, factual QA, and deep-search benchmarks, including GSM-Hard in the appendix. New comparisons and analyses reuse existing task coverage. v3's assertion that deep search is absent from training conflicts with its retained WebWalker training source and does not establish a coverage change.

E2.justification: v3 adds OPD, PRM-style step-reward GRPO, and ReLIFT in Table 8, plus DPO in Figure 5. It removes Qwen2.5-32B TIR from the eight-task comparison and removes student CoT Prompting, plain CoT Distillation, and Agent Prompting rows from the exact-match comparison. GRPO and ARPO are retained under clarified BC-prefixed names.

E3.justification: Reported WebWalker and xBench test sizes change from 100 and 200 to 200 and 100, respectively; the PDFs do not establish reruns. New comparisons specify a Qwen3-32B teacher for OPD, twice the training data for ReLIFT, and the same MPS data for DPO. Core metrics, training hyperparameters, and the eight-step limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a same-data DPO comparison testing the value of RL, a manual audit of 50 previously hard-to-teach cases distinguishing strategy improvement from generation instability, and a representative verification case. It also reports intervention token costs and a small reward-scale search. Existing component ablations, intervention-frequency analysis, and SFT data-scaling experiments are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 1 newly states that AIME24 and AIME25 results are averaged over five runs. v1 gives no corresponding run count, so this establishes new reporting rather than an explicit increase in runs. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests for these comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises SCoRe-RL's AIME24/AIME25 scores from 36.7/26.7 to 38.0/28.7 and its reported average from 50.8 to 52.3, alongside newly stated five-run averaging. Table 8 adds averages of 24.2 for OPD, 25.5 for step-reward GRPO, and 26.7 for ReLIFT against SCoRe-RL's retained 30.5. DPO, case-analysis, and token-cost findings are added; some exact-match values change, and GAIA difficulty-level results are removed. These are reporting changes, not an established same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The three compounding-error and rollout-variance bounds, their mathematical assumptions, and their proofs are preserved, moving from Appendix A to B. The new assumptions remark restates existing conditions and qualifies practical interpretation without changing the derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain student-centered correction data, capability-matched SFT, and short-horizon RL with localized rewards. Both versions claim that a 7B student approaches a 72B teacher across 12 benchmarks. The revised title and abstract retain this scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive qualifications about the conditional O(H) bound and dependence on teacher quality. It interprets hard-case improvements as strategy refinement and explains differences from PRM-style supervision, OPD, ReLIFT, and DPO. It also introduces the unresolved claim that deep-search data is absent from training despite listing WebWalker as a training source.

D1.justification: New Appendix E supplies the teacher's error-localization and correction prompts. v3 additionally documents the 10% hard-example allocation for RL, filtering of easy examples, Qwen3's non-thinking mode, reward-scale selection, and additional baseline settings. The code link points to a different repository. These substantially expand implementation disclosure; the earlier 35k seed total and GPU memory specification are omitted.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning against DAgger/HG-DAgger and distinguish SCoRe from LEMMA and process-reward approaches. New OPD, ReLIFT, cognitive-alignment, and DeepSeek-R1 references support additional comparisons and explanations. Numerous publication-metadata updates accompany these substantive additions.

P1.justification: v3 retitles and reorganizes the paper, moving Related Work before Background, expanding explanations of complete-trajectory review and correction validation, and separating ablations from hard-case analysis. The appendices are reorganized into five sections, with dedicated positioning and prompt sections. These changes materially reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is substantially redrawn; Table 1 is split between the main text and appendix; Table 2 removes GAIA subgroup columns; and the exact-match table is shortened. New displays include the hard-case example, additional baseline table, DPO chart, and two prompt figures.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct comparisons with several teacher-guided alternatives and did not provide the central MPS prompts. v3's Table 8, same-data DPO comparison, and full prompt templates substantially strengthen comparative validation and reproducibility. The manual case analysis, five-run AIME reporting, and explicit theoretical limitations further improve transparency. These gains outweigh the removed comparison detail, although unexplained test-size revisions and the contradictory deep-search training claim remain weaknesses.
